title: Islam Began as Something Strange, So Glad Tidings to the Strangers
behavior_type: الشعور بالاختلاف عن الأصدقاء بسبب الالتزام
reference_info: صحيح مسلم، حديث رقم 145، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه
text_original: بدأ الإسلام غريبًا وسيعود غريبًا كما بدأ، فطوبى للغرباء. رواه مسلم (145) عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه.
text_simplified: When your child feels like a stranger because he is the only one in his company who prays or observes hijab, teach him the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: «بدأ الإسلام غريبًا، وسيعود كما بدأ غريبًا، فطوبى للغرباء» — “Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being strange as it began, so glad tidings to the strangers.” (Sahih Muslim 145). Explain to him that differing from the majority in obedience to Allah is not a deficiency, but rather the praise with which the Prophet ﷺ promised the committed in every era.

review_defects.why: "بشّر" means "gave glad tidings to," not "promised," so the English loses the good-news nuance that is central to the hadith.
"The committed" as a standalone noun is an awkward calque from Arabic and reads unnaturally in English.
«بشّر» means 'gave glad tidings to' rather than 'promised'; the nuance of conveying good news is softened.
